statement.p: In this activity, we will use homogeneous coordinates and matrix transformations to move our character into a variety of poses.

li.p:
Since we regard our character as living in \real^3, we will consider matrix transformations defined by matrices
\left[\begin{array}{rrr} a \amp b \amp c \\ d \amp e \amp f \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \\ \end{array}\right] . Verify that such a matrix transformation transforms points in the plane z=1 into points in the same plane; that is, verify that
\left[\begin{array}{rrr} a \amp b \amp c \\ d \amp e \amp f \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \\ \end{array}\right] \threevec{x}{y}{1} = \threevec{x'}{y'}{1} . Express the coordinates of the resulting point x' and y' in terms of the coordinates of the original point x and y.

description.p: This interactive diagram has a set of six sliders across the top. In the top row are three sliders labelled a, b, and c. In the bottom row are three sliders labelled d, e, and f. The reader can move these sliders to define a matrix transformation defined by the matrix \begin{bmatrix}a \amp b \amp c \\ d \amp e \amp f \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \\ \end{bmatrix}.

Below the set of six sliders is a set of two diagrams. The left depicts the stick figure character that was introduced earlier. On the right is shown the result of applying the matrix transformation to the stick figure.
Furthermore, there are two buttons at the bottom of the diagram labelled Compose and Reset.

instructions.p: The diagram below allows you to choose parameters a, b, \ldots, f to define the matrix associated to the matrix \begin{bmatrix} a \amp b \amp c \\ d \amp e \amp f \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \\ \end{bmatrix}. The transformation's effect on our character is shown on the right.

li.p: Write a final scene to the movie and describe how to construct a sequence of matrix transformations that create your scene.

Notice that the entries c and f are responsible for the translation. Therefore, we need the matrix transformation defined by \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp 0 \amp 2 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp 1 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \\ \end{array}\right] .
We would like to reflect in the vertical axis so we use the matrix \left[\begin{array}{rrr} -1 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \\ \end{array}\right] .

The character is successively rotated by 45^\circ using the matrix
\left[\begin{array}{rrr} \cos(45^\circ) \amp -\sin(45^\circ) \amp 0 \\ \sin(45^\circ) \amp \sin(45^\circ) \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \\ \end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{rrr} \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \amp -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \amp 0 \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \amp \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \\ \end{array}\right] .

We first translate the character down two units using the matrix \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp -2 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \\ \end{array}\right] . Then we zoom in by uniformly stretching by a factor of 2 using the matrix \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 2 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 2 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \\ \end{array}\right] . The net effect is the transformation described by the matrix
\left[\begin{array}{rrr} 2 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 2 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \\ \end{array}\right] \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp -2 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \\ \end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 2 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 2 \amp -4 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \\ \end{array}\right]\text{.}

The shadow is first created using the shear
\left[\begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp 1 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \\ \end{array}\right] . Then the vertical scale is compressed using the matrix
\left[\begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp \frac12 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \\ \end{array}\right] .
